pages.text: Nodes and linkers crystallise into an open net; the pore across it is set by the linker's length. A pore that fits one target molecule holds it best. The solvent left in the pores must be driven off slowly - pulled out fast, its surface tension crushes them.
$(thing)Set$(): Linker length, Drying rate.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Crystal defects: the pore varies by ±0.02 Å·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): none beyond the recipe windows.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Faster drying, faster batches.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Pore size: d ≈ 0.8·L − 0.5 Å$(br)Fit to the target: e^(−((d − d_target)/0.4 Å)²)$(br)Pores intact: e^(−3·(rate − 0.3))
